capsuleTopic.title: Last Supper
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Passover · table · betrayal · bread · cup · service · farewell · remembrance
capsuleTopic.orientation: Enter the final meal through four distinct witnesses. Passover and covenant sources prepare the language; Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John preserve their own sequences; John’s farewell teaching and prayer deepen the night; Paul and later sources show how the meal is remembered, practiced, and compared.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow preparation, table fellowship, betrayal, bread, cup, service, love, departure, prayer, remembrance, participation, and future hope without blending the witnesses or turning every biblical meal into the Lord’s Supper.

passages.excerpt: “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may b…
passages.observation: Jesus prays for those who will believe through the disciples’ word, asks for unity that the world may believe, speaks of shared glory, desired presence, known name, and indwelling love.

passages.title: Jesus crosses the brook and meets the arresting party
passages.excerpt: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered. Now Judas, who betrayed him,…
passages.observation: Jesus enters a garden known to Judas, steps forward before soldiers and officers, identifies himself, protects the disciples, and tells Peter to put away the sword and names the Father’s cup.

passages.title: The accusers avoid defilement so they may eat Passover
passages.excerpt: They led Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and they themselves didn’t enter into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passove…
passages.observation: Jesus is led from Caiaphas to the Praetorium early; his accusers remain outside to avoid defilement and eat Passover while Pilate questions their accusation and execution demand.

passages.title: John names the preparation of Passover at sentencing
passages.excerpt: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.” Now it was the Preparation D…
passages.observation: Pilate sits on the judgment seat at the Stone Pavement; John identifies it as the preparation of Passover around noon before Jesus is delivered for crucifixion.

passages.title: Passover and unleavened bread become communal imagery
passages.excerpt: Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump? Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ,…
passages.observation: Paul warns that a little yeast leavens the whole lump, calls Christ the sacrificed Passover, and urges festival keeping with sincerity and truth rather than malice and wickedness.

passages.title: One cup and one bread mark participation and table allegiance
passages.excerpt: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry. I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say. The cup of blessing which we bless, isn’t it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we br…
passages.observation: Paul calls the community away from idolatry, names the cup and bread as participation in Christ, links one bread to one body, and contrasts the Lord’s table with the table of demons.

passages.title: Divisions make the gathering not the Lord’s Supper
passages.excerpt: But in giving you this command I don’t praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse. For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that…
passages.observation: Paul says the assembly does more harm than good, divisions expose approved people, private meals leave some hungry and others drunk, and the church of God is despised.

passages.title: Paul transmits what he received about the night of betrayal
passages.excerpt: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread. When he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “T…
passages.observation: Paul says he received and delivered the tradition: on the night betrayed Jesus took bread, gave thanks, named body and remembrance, then named the cup as new covenant and repeated remembrance until he comes.

passages.title: Examination, discernment, judgment, and waiting govern the meal
passages.excerpt: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way unworthy of the Lord will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let…
passages.observation: Paul warns about unworthy eating and drinking, calls for self-examination and body discernment, connects failure with weakness and death, and commands waiting for one another.

passages.title: The Jerusalem community persists in breaking bread
passages.excerpt: They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer. Fear came on every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apos…
passages.observation: The newly formed community continues in apostolic teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, prayers, shared possessions, temple life, household meals, praise, favor, and daily addition.

passages.title: The risen Jesus is recognized in breaking bread
passages.excerpt: They came near to the village where they were going, and he acted like he would go further. They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.”…
passages.observation: At Emmaus the travelers urge Jesus to stay; at table he takes, blesses, breaks, and gives bread, their eyes open, he vanishes, and they return to report recognition in the breaking of bread.

passages.title: Breaking bread frames an all-night gathering and restored life
passages.excerpt: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnig…
passages.observation: On the first day of the week disciples gather to break bread, Paul speaks until midnight, Eutychus falls and is taken up dead, Paul embraces him, breaks bread, continues talking, and the young man is brought alive.

passages.title: Hebrews quotes the promised new covenant
passages.excerpt: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law. For if that first covenant…
passages.observation: Hebrews argues for a better ministry and covenant, quotes Jeremiah’s promise to Israel and Judah, and concludes that calling it new makes the first old and near disappearance.

passages.title: Mediator, covenant, death, and blood are interpreted together
passages.excerpt: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been ca…
passages.observation: Hebrews calls Christ mediator of a new covenant, links death to redemption and inheritance, explains covenant inauguration through Moses, and says cleansing is generally by blood.

passages.title: One offering and the new-covenant promise are held together
passages.excerpt: Every priest indeed stands day by day serving and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins, but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat dow…
passages.observation: Hebrews contrasts repeated priestly service with Christ’s one offering, speaks of enemies, perfection, the Spirit’s Jeremiah quotation, forgiveness, and no further offering for sin.

passages.title: The risen Jesus prepares bread and fish by the sea
passages.excerpt: After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way. Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee,…
passages.observation: After an unsuccessful night, the risen Jesus directs a catch, prepares a charcoal fire with fish and bread, invites the disciples to breakfast, gives bread and fish, and is recognized.

passages.title: A wedding supper is announced in heavenly praise
passages.excerpt: I heard something like the voice of a great multitude, and like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of mighty thunders, saying, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God, the Almighty,…
passages.observation: A great multitude celebrates God’s reign, the Lamb’s marriage and prepared wife, blessing for those invited to the wedding supper, true words of God, and worship redirected from the angel to God.
